assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, and the subsequent identification of the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources, opened neutrino astronomy as a new window on the high-energy universe. It is a clear, original discovery enabled by an instrument conception, a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice, that many thought unrealistic. As an experimentalist who builds detectors for cosmic particles, I find the combination of instrumental audacity and a physics result that does not depend on interpretation especially compelling.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit lists only Francis Halzen, who conceived and led IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA over three decades. A one-person prize would be defensible on the instrument-leadership argument, but the discovery was made by a large collaboration, and I cannot independently verify from the supplied text how the committee would weigh other founding figures who are not in the credited names; the list does not permit adding anyone.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 high-energy starting-event result has been confirmed across several independent channels (through-going muons, cascades, tau-candidate analyses) and the 2018 multi-messenger association was followed by further source evidence, so the core discovery is stable. Timing is good: the field has matured past a single-event claim, though source-population questions remain open.
uncertainties: Whether a single named laureate is an adequate representation of a collaboration-scale discovery.

Individual source identifications (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) are statistically moderate compared with the diffuse-flux detection; I am relying on recollection of these significances rather than a fresh check.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and pushed by Ye to uncertainties and stabilities near 10^-18, is a transformative measurement technology. It has redefined the practical limits of timekeeping, enables relativistic geodesy at the centimetre level, and provides sensitivity to variations of constants and dark-matter signatures. The importance and originality are high, and the result is a textbook instrument-driven advance.
assessment.attribution: Katori (magic-wavelength concept, Sr clock realization) and Ye (precision, many-body clocks, comb-linked frequency transfer) are the evident principal contributors and form a clean two-person configuration. Other groups (for example ion-clock and Hg/Yb lattice efforts) contributed, but the supplied credit is narrow and coherent.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories have reproduced and surpassed the 10^-18 level, and international clock comparisons confirm it. The redefinition of the second is still pending, but that does not undermine the science. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of frequency-comb and ion-trap clock work (2005, 2012 prizes) may lead colleagues to consider this incremental.
Whether the committee would favour a broader clock prize including other lattice-clock pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators and its observation in HgTe quantum wells launched a field that connects band topology, spin-orbit physics and protected edge transport. Its influence extends through materials discovery, spintronics and quantum-device concepts. It is among the most important condensed-matter conceptual advances of the past two decades.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theoretical foundation and Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation in HgTe wells, following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's proposal, who are not in the credited names. Qi-Kun Xue is credited for the quantum anomalous Hall effect, a distinct compound discovery. I propose Kane and Molenkamp as the cleanest theory-plus-experiment pairing; Mele's and others' roles remain an unresolved credit question that this candidate's names do not let me settle.
assessment.maturity: Experiments have been repeated in several materials (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi2Se3-class compounds, QAH systems). The interpretation is stable and mature, although some quantization claims in 2D systems have been less clean than the original theory suggests.
uncertainties: Competing candidate entries (B048, B045) split credit for the same field; I cannot tell which framing the committee would favour.
Imperfect edge-conductance quantization in HgTe is a known caveat and I did not verify the current state of the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles, and the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle bilayer graphene, created the field of moire quantum materials with tunable strongly correlated physics. The result is original, was widely reproduced within a short time, and has generated fractional Chern insulators, orbital magnetism and a platform for exploring correlation physics.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gave the quantitative prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery and the 'twistronics' control. Rafi Bistritzer was the first author of the theory and could reasonably be part of a three-person prize; I propose the senior theorist and experimentalist, with the third slot an open question. Other groups (Dean, Young, Efetov and others) are outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduction across many laboratories and substrates has been rapid and convincing, but the nature of superconductivity and the correlated phases is still debated. The discovery is solid, though a prize might be seen as slightly early compared with the older candidates.
uncertainties: Premature relative to older, better-understood discoveries; the pairing mechanism is unresolved.
Allocation among Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero, and the possible role of Kim, Dean and others not in the credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of X-ray and optical afterglows of gamma-ray bursts with BeppoSAX, followed by redshift measurements, settled a thirty-year debate and placed the bursts at cosmological distances. This was a definitive, originality-rich discovery that created modern transient and multi-messenger astronomy. As a scientist working on gamma-ray instrumentation and polarimetry, I recognise how decisive precise localisation by a wide-field monitor plus rapid follow-up was.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX Wide Field Cameras and Gamma-Ray Burst Monitor localisation of GRB 970228; Kulkarni's group provided the radio and optical redshift evidence that made the cosmological case. Jan van Paradijs, a key figure in the optical counterpart discovery, is deceased and cannot be honoured, and I recall that others (Frail, Djorgovski, Metzger) are not in the credit list. The three-person configuration is reasonable but the Kulkarni versus other optical/radio contributors question is not fully resolved.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of data, thousands of bursts and the GW170817 association confirm the cosmological nature of GRBs. This is very mature; if anything the delay risks losing the surviving discoverers.
uncertainties: Which optical and radio contributors are honoured given the loss of van Paradijs.
I did not verify the precise attribution history of the first optical transient versus the X-ray afterglow.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum computation with trapped ions and Blatt's experimental realisation of high-fidelity gates, entanglement, teleportation and digital quantum simulation shaped the leading platform for quantum information processing. The results are original, precise and have clear lasting influence on both fundamental quantum physics and technology.
assessment.attribution: The Cirac-Zoller pairing is the core theory contribution; Blatt's group provided the principal experimental demonstrations in Innsbruck, with Wineland's NIST group (not credited here and already recognised in 2012) also central. A theory-theory-experiment trio fits the supplied names, but Cirac and Zoller also appear in other candidates and the committee must avoid double allocation.
assessment.maturity: Well-reproduced across several groups and now supported by commercial systems; the underlying science is mature. The partial overlap with the 2012 prize may argue for waiting.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's recognition and with the optical-lattice and Rydberg candidates that credit the same theorists.
Whether trapped-ion computing is viewed as a mature physics discovery or an evolving technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned matter-wave coherence into a precision measurement tool, used for gravimetry, tests of the equivalence principle, measurements of the gravitational constant and the fine-structure constant, and proposals for gravitational-wave and dark-matter detection. As someone who designs detectors for fundamental measurements, I value the combination of conceptual clarity and instrumental refinement.
assessment.attribution: Bordé (theory and early Ramsey-Bordé interferometer), Pritchard (first matter-wave interferometers with atoms and molecules) and Kasevich (laser-pulse interferometers, large-momentum-transfer, inertial sensing) form a defensible three-person set; Schmiedmayer's atom-chip work is a further contributor and the credit is spread over four names, so allocation is contested, and Chu's 1990s work is not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories now operate atom interferometers, but the most ambitious aims (gravitational-wave detection, definitive equivalence-principle tests) are not yet achieved. The technology is mature; the physics payoff is still incomplete.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit across four names and the missing contributions of other pioneers.
Whether the scientific discovery is clear enough compared with the instrument-development contribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of radioactively powered kilonova emission and its observation following GW170817 established neutron-star mergers as a major r-process site, a long-standing nuclear astrophysics question. It is a rare case where theory, observation and gravitational-wave multi-messenger astronomy converge.
assessment.attribution: Metzger and Kasen provided the central theoretical framework, and Foley's team was among the groups that discovered and characterised the optical counterpart; many other observational teams (Swope, DECam, Hubble and others) and early theory work (Li and Paczynski) lie outside the credited names, so attribution is difficult and could be contested.
assessment.maturity: GW170817 is a single event in this regime, and the r-process interpretation, including the amount of heavy-element production, still relies on modelling. A broader sample from future runs would strengthen it, so the discovery may be a little early.
uncertainties: Single well-observed event; heavy-element yields are model dependent.
Credit allocation between theorists, the many observational discovery teams, and the 2017 gravitational-wave prize recipients.
